turns.content: What should I do with my itemised receipt used for a Deloitte event?

expected_output: Explains that events — regardless of value — must be paid through Swift Accounts Payable with a valid tax invoice or receipt and a signed contract, not claimed as a standard Amex expense. Confirms the itemised tax invoice should be retained/attached for the event claim. Tone is concise, conversational, and policy-accurate.

metadata.case_name: Standard query — itemised receipt for a Deloitte event

turns.content: Which card should I use to pay for a $180 team lunch?
Got it. And when will I actually get reimbursed?

expected_output: First turn confirms business expenses under $2,500 should be paid on the Deloitte personal-liability Amex card. Second turn explains reimbursement is aligned to Amex statement dates once the claim is correctly submitted and approved, with the individual responsible for claiming in the correct timeframe.

metadata.case_name: Standard query — payment card threshold then reimbursement timing

turns.content: I lost the receipt for a $60 client dinner. Can I still claim it?

expected_output: Explains that a missing receipt affidavit may be submitted only in extremely limited circumstances and used at most once or twice per calendar year, and that Deloitte reserves the right to challenge a claim without a receipt. Does not present it as a routine option.

metadata.case_name: Edge case — lost receipt / missing receipt affidavit

turns.content: I forgot to submit an expense from about three months ago. Can I still claim it?
Also, the vendor didn't take Amex so I used my personal card — is that allowed?

expected_output: First turn explains expenses should be submitted within 30 days and no more than 60 days; beyond 60 days requires Firm CFO approval on extenuating grounds, and late submission or lack of policy knowledge are not valid reasons. Second turn explains personal-card ('Out of Pocket') use is by exception only when a vendor does not accept Amex, requires a valid reason, and needs a valid itemised tax receipt regardless of value.

metadata.case_name: Edge case — late submission then personal-card out-of-pocket

turns.content: How many annual leave days do I have left this year?

expected_output: Recognises the question is outside expense-policy scope, apologises briefly, does not fabricate an answer, and redirects the user to raise an Expense incident in ServiceNow and to the Expense Policy Hub. May offer the feedback form.

Fine. Then how do I reset my Concur password?

expected_output: First turn declines to approve or action the claim (read-only behaviour) and redirects appropriately. Second turn recognises the Concur password reset is out of scope and redirects to ServiceNow, without attempting the action.

turns.content: How do I get my money back?

expected_output: Recognises the request is vague and asks 2-3 clarifying questions (e.g. expense type, payment method, claim stage) rather than guessing at an answer.

turns.content: I need help with an expense.
I paid for a client dinner on my Amex last week and want to claim it.
Anything else I should know before I submit?

expected_output: First turn asks clarifying questions. After the user specifies an Amex client-dinner claim, the agent gives grounded guidance: attach the itemised tax invoice in Concur, code client-related expenses to the client engagement code, and submit monthly within 60 days.
